According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 633,700 middle school teachers, excluding special and career or technical education, were employed in 2024, declining to a projected 621,300 by 2034. That represents roughly 12,400 fewer jobs, with about 40,500 openings per year and median annual pay of approximately $63,000 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace middle school teachers, but it will free substantial desk time. AI is taking over repetitive work such as lesson preparation, grading, and analysis of student learning that consumes about half of teachers' energy. Yet middle school teaching has never been only about explaining answers correctly. Machines cannot manage classroom discipline, support adolescent emotions, or build trust between families and schools face to face. Teaching that merely reads from textbooks faces elimination, not the teaching profession.

Study teacher education and earn a teaching credential, but consider subjects with structural shortages, including music, physical education, art, psychology, and information technology, rather than focusing only on Chinese, mathematics, and English. A teaching credential is a firm requirement, and non-education majors need teaching-practice experience. Highlight classroom leadership, communication, and teaching outcomes on your résumé. Private schools and tutoring organizations also provide entry points before pursuing public-school roles.
